author: AAAGamesEU
quote:
Grand Theft Auto VI is a monumental open-world achievement that sets a new benchmark for environmental detail and grounded storytelling, even though its core shooting and driving mechanics still feel noticeably dated.

The Good• Unmatched World Design: The state of Leonida, centered around a vibrant Vice City, bursts with life, dynamic weather, and organic random events that make exploration endlessly rewarding.• Grounded Narrative: Rockstar trades its usual over-the-top satire for an intimate, surprisingly emotional crime drama following Lucia and Jason's struggle for a fresh start.• Smarter Law Enforcement: Police now remember your face, outfit, and vehicle, turning escapes into tense, tactical getaways where changing clothes or wearing a mask actually matters.• Tactical Realism: Borrowing from Red Dead Redemption 2, limiting your loadout to two main weapons and adding a focus-aim ability makes firefights feel much more deliberate.

The Bad• Slow Opening Hours: The campaign takes roughly six to eight hours to build up its characters before throwing you into your first major shootout.• Dated Controls and Gunplay: Despite cinematic set pieces, the cover system, shooting mechanics, and occasionally sluggish vehicle handling feel stuck in the past.• Missing Side Activities: Longtime fans will notice the absence of classic franchise staples like real estate purchases, the stock market, and taxi missions.• 30 FPS Cap: Even on mid-gen console hardware like the PS5 Pro, the frame rate is locked at 30 FPS, though rock-solid pacing keeps it visually smooth.
